source.title: Inconsistency, Instability, and Generalization Gap of Deep Neural Network Training

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization gaps and tests different output-discrepancy and sharpness measures as predictors; it does not test the specific interventions or magnitude-aware measure named in the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows report the study's own measured relationships between generalization gap and inconsistency or sharpness. Cited results from prior studies are excluded. Figure-based correlations in Sections 3.1 and 3.2 are described qualitatively in the text; no numeric values were reconstructed from plots.
record.test_reason: The study tests output inconsistency as a generalization-gap predictor and compares it with unscaled 1-sharpness and Hessian magnitude. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or test any other listed version. Its related empirical findings therefore fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that output inconsistency and instability predict generalization gaps, that inconsistency is more reliable than the tested local sharpness measures, and that encouraging consistency improves test performance. Their empirical predictiveness finding depends on low final randomness; it does not establish superiority over magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures output inconsistency and instability and compares them with sharpness; it does not reproduce the listed interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictiveness of DP depended on low randomness in the final state: with constant SGD without iterate averaging, DP was predictive only among procedures sharing a learning rate; with iterate averaging or vanishing learning rate, it was predictive across procedures. Disagreement's relation to test error differed by dataset and training condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Across ten cases, inconsistency yields lower leave-one-out generalization-gap prediction error than training-loss 1-sharpness or Hessian magnitude.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the studied training objectives and models with low final randomness, output inconsistency predicts cross-entropy generalization gaps better than the tested unscaled local sharpness measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Inconsistency plus instability predicts generalization gaps across learning rates with iterate averaging or vanishing learning rates; without averaging under constant SGD, predictiveness holds mainly within a shared learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usefulness of output discrepancy as a generalization-gap predictor depends on final training randomness.

record.problems: The authors note resource constraints limited diversity of training procedures, especially in CIFAR-100 and ImageNet experiments. The empirical correlations are not causal evidence. Section 3.2 evaluates a limited set of metrics; the authors acknowledge other predictive metrics may exist. Some correlation findings are presented in plots without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Section 3.1 figure-based correlations among DP, inconsistency, instability, generalization gap, disagreement, and test error were not transcribed as numeric rows because values are shown only in figures; their qualitative descriptions are reflected in method_sensitivity. Table 3 rows for Hessian and dev-loss sharpness metrics were omitted to stay focused on the main inconsistency-versus-sharpness comparison.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels with natural-label training and held-out accuracy.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison under a specified tuning budget.
Batch sizes vary in Section 3.1, but no reported comparison establishes their effect on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout is fixed in one setting; no dropout intervention or removal comparison is reported.

No magnitude-aware weight perturbations, perturbation tolerance before training error rises, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. The tested 1-sharpness and Hessian measures do not operationalize this version.
No removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All twenty numeric values match Table 3. These rows describe the study's predictor comparison and should remain outside evidence for V1–V8. A higher prediction error than inconsistency does not by itself show absent or reversed sharpness correlation. No omitted result operationalizes a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization were not compared.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures for this claim.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
The study compares inconsistency with 1-sharpness and Hessian magnitude, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight perturbations scaled to weight magnitudes.
